utility_name: Consolidated Edison Co of New York (Con Edison)
rule_summary: Follows the statewide SIR for process and timelines, but its territory is dominated by underground secondary-network and spot-network grid, which changes what interconnection actually costs. Con Edison publishes CESIR cost ranges of up to about $20,000 for inverter-based systems and about $27,000 for rotating machines. On spot/isolated networks the default is a reverse-power relay that prevents export; since 2012 Con Edison offers Communications Aided Tripping (CAT) - insensitive network-protector settings plus SCADA, anti-islanding and DNP3 telemetry - to allow export on network service, at a project cost on the order of $100,000. Con Edison states it is the only utility in the nation allowing export on network service. Interconnection portal split at 50 kW-AC (Small DG vs Large DG); for hybrid projects the portal is chosen by export capability rather than combined nameplate. 2026 Customer Benefit Contribution: net-metered PV $1.29/kW-mo residential and $1.47/kW-mo small commercial; Value Stack PV $0.65 and $1.03.
ic_study_trigger_kw: In underground secondary network areas a CESIR may be required even for systems at or below 50 kW (SIR Sec I.C Exception 1); Con Edison-published CESIR cost up to ~$20,000 inverter-based and ~$27,000 rotating machine.
non_export_option: Yes - reverse power relay preventing export is Con Edison's traditional approach on spot and isolated networks; CAT is the paid alternative that permits export.
grid_charging_allowed: Yes - see state row. Con Edison requires charging kW (peak kW/kVA needed to charge) to be stated in the application scope of work; if it exceeds the local service, service upgrades may be required.
standby_charge: Standby Service under General Rule 20, plus the Rider Q Standby Pilot Rate Program (customer-selected contract demand and As-Used demand period) and SC-11 Buy-Back Service (LBMP, grossed up by 1.066 for secondary-level deliveries). Published standby rates (as of retrieval): residential contract demand $6.05/kW plus $20 customer charge; small business $8.77/kW plus $33; large commercial low-tension under 1,500 kW $9.18/kW plus $71.
standby_threshold_kw: 50 - customers with Contract Demand below 50 kW are reported exempt from mandatory Standby Service billing under General Rule 20.3, as are customers whose on-site generation nameplate is no more than 15% of maximum potential demand served from all sources. This aligns the standby threshold with the SIR's 50 kW expedited/large-project boundary. Threshold is SECONDARY-sourced - not read in the General Rule 20 tariff leaf.
storage_specific_notes: Con Edison states that SC1 residential customers under 25 kW-AC and SC2 small commercial customers under 2 MW-AC who install an ESS after 2017-03-10 receive Phase One NEM compensation, and that residential and small commercial customers are eligible to pair grid-parallel storage with solar and take service under Phase One NEM - i.e. adding a battery does not by itself force a move off Phase One NEM. Storage may only be added to a Phase One NEM system if it is paired with another Phase One NEM-eligible technology. Adding an ESS to an existing DG facility is filed as a Battery Energy Storage application with SIR Appendix K; a new PV plus new storage project is filed as a single Hybrid application. Metering: three acceptable hybrid configurations - exclusive ESS charge from PV, PV export only, and separate metering; the PSC approved a three-meter configuration for hybrid ESS in Case 18-E-0081, Order Modifying Standardized Interconnection Requirements issued 2018-04-19. Technologies behind one meter that are credited under different rate structures require specialized metering and/or relaying. NOTE: this guide is Version 4, July 2022, aligned to the May 2022 SIR - re-verify against the 2026-02-09 SIR.

utility_name: Long Island Power Authority / PSEG Long Island
rule_summary: Does NOT follow the New York State SIR. LIPA is a state authority outside PSC jurisdiction and PSL 66-j/66-l do not apply to it. Interconnection runs under LIPA's own Small Generator Interconnection Procedures (SGIP), an addendum to LIPA's Tariff for Electric Service, administered by PSEG Long Island as LIPA's agent, with a separate Smart Grid SGIP (SGSGIP) track. Scope is broader than the state SIR: distributed generation facilities with a nameplate rating of 10 MW or less aggregated on the customer side of the point of common coupling, versus 5 MW under the PSC SIR. Applications go through PSEG Long Island's Interconnection Online Application Portal (live since 2021-02-12). Separate PSEG Long Island technical requirements documents cover DER up to 500 kVA and above 500 kVA.
ic_application_fee: SGIP application fee $750 for 50 kW to 5 MW and $750 for 5 MW to 10 MW, payable to PSEG Long Island (SGIP Application Instructions, https://www.psegliny.com/aboutpseglongisland/ratesandtariffs/sgip/applications). Fee for systems under 50 kW not verified.
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear - LIPA SGIP and tariff not verified on whether a battery may charge from the grid and still export or earn credit
storage_specific_notes: Not verified. LIPA's storage-specific interconnection and compensation provisions, and whether adding storage to an existing LIPA net-metered system changes compensation, were not established in this pass.
